headline: North-West revenue drop tracks fulfilment delays and enterprise account loss.
body: Fulfilment SLA slipped nearly 4%, tied to WH-07 backlog and repeated late deliveries [E1]. Enterprise accounts fell 7%, with two named accounts shifting volume to a competitor citing missed SLAs [E2]. Complaints rose in step with these delays, consistent with churn risk flagged directly by customers [E3]. A separate drop in marketing conversion moved too but has no supporting evidence yet and should be treated as a lead, not a cause.

actions.action: Track WH-07 backlog and dispatch delay daily
actions.expected_impact: Confirms whether SLA recovery follows capacity fix
actions.monitoring: Daily WH-07 backlog count and SLA %

actions.expected_impact: Detects further volume loss before renewal
actions.monitoring: Order volume from Meridian and Kalinga accounts

actions.action: Watch complaint rate and delivery-promise accuracy
actions.expected_impact: Flags if messaging changes reduce complaints

what_could_change: Evidence tying marketing conversion drop to actual funnel data, or SLA recovery after 3PL overflow, would sharpen this diagnosis.
caveats: Marketing conversion decline is unexplained and not yet backed by direct evidence; treat as a lead only.
clarifying_question: Is the WH-07 backlog isolated to North-West or spreading to other warehouses?
